Compute endorsement rates across a range of thresholds

threshold_sensitivity.Rd

Computes the endorsement rate per item at each cut point, which shows how much of an item's rate is a property of the documents and how much is a property of where the cut falls.

Usage

threshold_sensitivity(
  results,
  target = NULL,
  thresholds = seq(0.1, 0.9, by = 0.1),
  value = c("prob_renorm", "prob")
)

Arguments

results

A fathom_results object from measure() or read_checkpoints().

target

A string naming the label counted as endorsement. Defaults to the first.

thresholds

A numeric vector of cut points to evaluate. Default is seq(0.1, 0.9, by = 0.1).

value

A string naming the probability column to threshold. Defaults to "prob_renorm", the figure after the label probabilities have been rescaled to sum to 1. That is the question a cut point is usually being asked to answer, which is whether documents pile up near the boundary between your labels, and it is the quantity everything downstream compares against.

"prob" is the raw probability, so a sweep over it also moves with mass the model spent outside your labels. That confounds two things, and a rate that shifts under it may be reporting compliance rather than the corpus. Use it when the claim is about whether the model committed.

Value

A tibble with one row per item and threshold, items in instrument order and thresholds ascending within an item. The message printed alongside is a ranking rather than a table and stays widest swing first.

  • item is the question name.

  • threshold is the cut point, one row per value in thresholds.

  • n counts the documents scored on this item. The same on every row of an item, since the cut point changes which documents count as endorsing and not how many were asked.

  • n_endorse counts the documents whose value for target reached the cut.

  • endorse is n_endorse over the documents with a value to cut. A document where no label appeared has no prob_renorm, so under the default it leaves this denominator, and endorse is n_endorse over n only when no such document exists. That is the split item_report() makes between endorse_renorm and endorse. This is the column to read down, and the spread from its smallest to largest value within an item is what the message ranks on.

More than two labels

This assumes a two-label instrument. Thresholding one label's probability asks whether that label is present, which is a question only a two-label instrument answers. On an instrument of three or more labels the labels compete for one pool of probability, so a label can win at 0.3 and lose at 0.6, and its rate at a series of cut points describes the arithmetic rather than the corpus. On a scored instrument the labels are levels of a scale, and a cut point on one level is not a measurement of anything.

The function does not refuse, because a cut point is the whole subject here and there is no other quantity for it to report. It runs on whatever you pass and the figures will be arithmetically correct.

See also

item_report() for the winner distribution, and for mean_expected on a scored instrument, which needs no cut.

Examples

# Results from a real run ship with the package, so this needs no server.
p <- system.file("extdata", "vignette_results.rds", package = "fathom")
baked <- readRDS(p)
threshold_sensitivity(baked$res_indep, target = "YES")
#> 
#> Note     Endorsement swing across the range, widest first.
#>          mixed     0.02
#>          negative  0.02
#>          positive  0.00
#> # A tibble: 27 × 5
#>    item     threshold     n n_endorse endorse
#>    <chr>        <dbl> <int>     <int>   <dbl>
#>  1 negative       0.1   100        47    0.47
#>  2 negative       0.2   100        47    0.47
#>  3 negative       0.3   100        47    0.47
#>  4 negative       0.4   100        47    0.47
#>  5 negative       0.5   100        47    0.47
#>  6 negative       0.6   100        46    0.46
#>  7 negative       0.7   100        46    0.46
#>  8 negative       0.8   100        46    0.46
#>  9 negative       0.9   100        45    0.45
#> 10 positive       0.1   100        42    0.42
